title: Reinforced Concrete Design to EC2
whyItMatters: Reinforced concrete relies on tension steel and compression concrete working together with adequate bond, anchorage, cover, and ductility. Furthermore, early-age RC slabs are often critical during construction striking and backpropping.
introduction: Composite steel-concrete behaviour, strain compatibility, ductile under-reinforced flexural design, shear links, anchorage and lap lengths, slabs, punching shear, columns, durability cover, and temporary propping/backpropping.
objectives: Explain RC composite behaviour, cracked vs uncracked sections, neutral axis depth limit (x/d <= 0.45), and ductile under-reinforced design.
Design singly and doubly reinforced beams for flexure, variable-strut shear links, anchorage, laps, curtailment, and span-to-effective-depth deflection control.
Analyse one-way and two-way slabs, flat slab punching shear, and RC columns under axial load plus moment (including slenderness awareness).
Assess construction-stage formwork striking, prop loads, and multi-storey backpropping onto immature RC slabs.
learningGate: Produce a complete beam and slab design including reinforcement sketch, cover, laps and buildability check.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the dimensionless flexural factor K = M_Ed / (b * d^2 * fck).
questions.prompt: A rectangular RC beam has width b = 300 mm, effective depth d = 500 mm, and concrete cylinder strength fck = 30 MPa. Under an ultimate bending moment M_Ed = 225 kNm (225 x 10^6 Nmm), calculate K.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why Eurocode 2 limits the neutral axis depth ratio x/d (e.g. x/d <= 0.45 in the UK NA).
questions.prompt: Why does reinforced concrete design limit the neutral axis depth ratio x/d (to 0.45 for fck <= 50 MPa with zero redistribution in the UK NA) before requiring compression reinforcement?
questions.assumptions: Consider strain compatibility between eps_cu = 0.0035 at the top fibre and tensile strain in the bottom steel.
options: To guarantee an under-reinforced section where the tension steel yields with large visible deflections and cracking before the compression concrete crushes suddenly and brittlely
By applying the unfactored characteristic Serviceability Limit State action combination directly to the gross cross-sectional area without accounting for partial mater.
By assuming a uniform linear-elastic stress distribution across the gross flange and web elements while neglecting rotational restraint compatibility, eccentric she.
Because concrete has higher tensile strength than steel
questions.explanation: Limiting x/d ensures that by the time the extreme concrete compression fibre reaches its ultimate crushing strain (0.0035), the tension steel has yielded well into its ductile plateau.

questions.learningObjective: Identify what happens when K exceeds K' (0.168) in a rectangular beam.
questions.prompt: If a beam’s factored moment gives K = M_Ed / (b * d^2 * fck) = 0.210 > K' = 0.168 and the section size cannot be increased, what must the engineer provide?
questions.assumptions: Consider singly vs doubly reinforced concrete sections.
options: Simply add more tension steel in the bottom without any compression steel, letting x/d exceed 0.75, assuming that because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel
Compression reinforcement (As2) in the top compression zone restrained by links, together with additional tension reinforcement to balance the couple above K'

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
questions.explanation: When K > K', the concrete compression block alone cannot balance the moment while keeping x/d <= 0.45; top compression steel (restrained against buckling by links) is required.

questions.learningObjective: Identify best practice for locating reinforcement laps in RC beams and slabs.
questions.prompt: Where should tension reinforcement lap splices ideally be located in a flexural member, and why?
questions.assumptions: Consider bond demand, cracking, and congestion.
options: Always 100% lapped at exact midspan of a simply supported beam with zero cover, assuming that it redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling

Away from plastic hinges and peak bending moment zones (staggering laps where possible), because lapping all bars at the point of maximum tensile stress creates severe congestion and high splitting bond demand

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages
questions.explanation: Lapping bars in regions of lower bending stress and staggering laps reduces local tensile bond splitting forces and concrete placement congestion.

moduleAssessmentQuestions.learningObjective: Explain why concrete compression strut capacity V_Rd,max must be checked even when shear links are provided.
moduleAssessmentQuestions.prompt: Why can you not simply keep adding more and more vertical shear links to carry an arbitrarily large shear force in a thin-webbed RC beam?
moduleAssessmentQuestions.assumptions: Consider Diagonal Compression Failure of the concrete web.
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel
If the diagonal compressive stress in the concrete web struts exceeds V_Rd,max, the concrete web crushes before the steel shear links yield

hints: First Hint (Governing Structural Principle: Pass the Module 14 Learning Gate: Produce a buildable, code-compliant RC design.): Reinforced concrete flexure equates the internal concrete compression block C_c and tension bar force T_s across lever arm z, limiting neutral axis depth x/d <= 0.45 (K <= K′ = 0.167) to ensure ductile steel yielding.

Second Hint (Analytical Elimination Criterion): Evaluate K = M_Ed / (b · d² · f_ck) in consistent (N, mm) units; verify K <= 0.167, determine lever arm z <= 0.95d, and calculate tension steel area A_s,req = M_Ed / (f_yd · z) where f_yd = f_yk / 1.15. Eliminate distractors that violate equilibrium, confuse elastic stiffness (E·I) with yield strength (f_y), or misapply Eurocode limit-state rules (Ref: Mosley Ch. 4, §4.1–4.6 & BS EN 1992-1-1 Cl. 3.1.7, Cl. 6.1).
